question: How was teixobactin, an antibiotic announced in 2015, found in soil that had been searched for decades?
answer: By growing bacteria that refuse to grow in a laboratory. Most soil microbes never form colonies on a dish, so earlier hunts had sampled only a small minority. A team led by Kim Lewis sealed soil bacteria in a device buried back in the soil, the iChip. A newly cultured species, Eleftheria terrae, made teixobactin.
move: When a well-searched place runs dry, question the method of searching.
reference: Ling et al., A new antibiotic kills pathogens without detectable resistance, Nature, 2015
